transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-12-02
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Emily Zhao (Oakwood Head of Security), Marcus Lee (Oakwood IT Ops), Dr. Naveen Patel (Oakwood CISO)

Summary: High level SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture review. Customer requests Trust Center access, controls mapping, KMS/BYOK options, audit log retention and SIEM integration, and data residency confirmations. Agreed next steps to share reports and schedule technical deep dive.

Topics: SOC 2/ISO reports, Trust Center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, audit logs/streaming, encryption/KMS/BYOK, data residency options, Redwood Dedicated vs Private, timeline for procurement.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jared from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Emily: Hi Jared, thanks. Good. We're in the middle of vendor assessments, so wanted to go through SOC 2 and ISO posture specifically.
[00:15] Marcus: Yeah we have a questionnaire and a few must-haves around KMS, key custody, audit logs, and data residency.
[00:21] Priya: Awesome. We'll try to surface the Trust Center artifacts and then dig into the mapping to your control set. Quick note - we'll probably reference our hosted offering, Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private depending on residency needs.
[00:31] Dr. Naveen: Good. We run in three jurisdictions, some PHI-like data and state-regulated records, so we need clarity on where data lives and how keys are managed.
[00:40] Jared: Totally. To set expectations, we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate via the Trust Center link. For deeper things like BYOK / HSM we've got options in Redwood Private that let you bring keys and integrate with your KMS - we'll cover that.
[00:52] Emily: When you say Trust Center link, is that a shared portal or single zip bundle? We need to save artifacts to our GRC.
[00:59] Jared: It's a secure portal with per-customer access. We'll provide a download bundle for the reports, plus the controls mapping template.
[01:06] Marcus: Great. For encryption we have a requirement: customer-managed keys or at least a deterministic envelope encryption using our KMS. We prefer BYOK.
[01:15] Priya: Understood. Redwood supports both customer-managed keys and our managed KMS. For Redwood Private we can do BYOK and HSM-backed keys with rotation policies. For hosted we offer KMS with tenant isolation, but BYOK requires Private deployment or dedicated HSM integration.
[01:29] Emily: Is there an EKM option for cloud providers? We use AWS KMS and a corporate EKM.
[01:35] Priya: Yes - for AWS we can integrate with your KMS via cross-account policies or use EKM for dedicated hardware. There's some differences depending on whether you choose Dedicated vs Private. Dedicated is hosted in our infra but gives isolated GPU pools and more control; Private gives you control plane in your VPC and full BYOK.
[01:49] Dr. Naveen: What about audit logs? We need immutable logs, retention for 7 years for some records, and real-time streaming to our SIEM for certain events.
[01:58] Jared: We have audit logs and the Redwood Console exposes per-route logs and traces. For long retention and streaming we can set up log export to your S3 (or GCS) bucket and integrate with your SIEM via Firehose or equivalent.
[02:11] Marcus: Do you support CloudTrail-style native logs or is it application-level logs?
[02:16] Priya: We provide structured audit events for auth, admin actions, model deploys, and data access. For infrastructure-level events (like kernel or hypervisor?) we can provide cloud provider logs if you're on Private; for hosted we provide extensive app audit events and export capabilities.
[02:29] Emily: Any gap around RBAC and SSO? We need SAML SSO and role-based access that maps to our IAM groups.
[02:36] Jared: Yes, we support SSO via SAML/SCIM provisioning and RBAC with role templates that can be mapped to your groups. Priya can go into the mapping details in the technical dive.
[02:45] Priya: Quick note - SCIM provisioning helps keep group membership in sync. We also have org-level roles and project-level roles; some customers map their security admins to org-admin and restrict deployment permissions.
[02:56] Marcus: For audit purposes we want to capture who invoked inference on certain models and the payload identifiers. Is that possible without capturing PII?
[03:05] Priya: Yes, we can log request IDs, model versions, and token counts without storing raw inputs. For regulated data we suggest prefix/KV caching with redaction and optionally tokenization on ingestion.
[03:16] Emily: Are there known caveats with prefix/KV cache and PHI? I saw notes about KV cache in your docs but wanted to confirm.
[03:23] Priya: Good question. KV cache is in-memory for active sessions; persistent caches are disabled for PHI workloads unless explicitly configured with approved controls. For Private deployments you control that behavior.
[03:34] Jared: Also, for HIPAA-like data we suggest Private or Dedicated with encryption at rest and client-managed keys. The hosted plan can be configured but doesn't give you the same isolation guarantees.
[03:45] Dr. Naveen: Okay. Regarding controls mapping - can you provide a mapping to our SOC 2 criteria and ISO clauses? We have our vendor risk team that needs the mapping.
[03:54] Jared: We'll share a controls mapping template that aligns Redwood controls to SOC 2 CC1-CC6 and ISO 27001 Annex A controls. Priya can annotate where we have compensating controls or where Private fulfills additional requirements.
[04:05] Priya: We'll flag which controls are in scope for the hosted environment versus Dedicated/Private. Some physical and personnel controls fall outside hosted scope and are in Dedicated/Private or require customer attestations.
[04:17] Marcus: For SOC 2 evidence - do you provide sysadmin logs and change management artifacts?
[04:22] Priya: We can provide evidence packages including change control summaries, patching cadence, and vulnerability scans as part of the SOC 2 bundle. Some pipeline artifacts are redacted for security, but auditors get the necessary attestations.
[04:33] Emily: What about third-party subservice organizations? We need to know if any critical control depends on partners.
[04:39] Jared: The SOC 2 report will list subservice orgs. Typically cloud provider dependencies are noted; we can call out any managed infra or monitoring vendors.
[04:46] Dr. Naveen: On KMS rotation: does Redwood force rotation or can we define rotation windows?
[04:51] Priya: If you're using customer-managed keys, rotation is under your control. For Redwood-managed keys we rotate per our key rotation policy, and we can provide rotation docs and logs for audit.
[05:02] Marcus: For forensic needs, can we get raw access logs or is it only aggregated? We may need packet-level logs for a while.
[05:09] Jared: Packet-level is typically handled at the VPC/network level. For Private deployments you can mirror traffic and capture at your side; hosted customers can request extended logs but packet-level may not be feasible. We'll document the boundary in the controls mapping.
[05:21] Emily: Do you provide pen test results?
[05:24] Priya: We have summary pen test findings in the compliance package. For deeper distro we can arrange an NDA and share more details.
[05:31] Dr. Naveen: How does Redwood handle data deletion requests and retention? We have retention policies where certain datasets must be deleted after X days.
[05:38] Jared: We support retention policies via API and console - you can configure TTL for stored artifacts. For requests we have processes and audit logs for deletions. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private with customer-side archival controls.
[05:52] Emily: One more on data residency: our legal needs to know where tokens and model outputs are persisted. Are model artifacts ever stored outside of the region?
[06:00] Priya: Model artifacts for hosted are in our region-specific infra unless you select cross-region replication. For Private you control where model weights and artifacts live. We'll include region mapping in the trust center docs.
[06:12] Marcus: For the SIEM integration, is there a standard schema? We'll want fields like actor, action, model_version, request_id, timestamp.
[06:19] Priya: Yes - we emit structured JSON events with those fields. We'll send the event schema in the follow-up and a sample CloudWatch/FluentD mapping.
[06:28] Jared: Quick pause - I want to call out typical red flags we see: customers often assume hosted gives full BYOK and full log mirroring; that's really a Private deployment feature. We'll call out the differences in the controls mapping.
[06:41] Emily: That helps. In procurement sometimes security insists on explicit statements. Will your SOC 2 report explicitly say anything about BYOK availability?
[06:49] Priya: SOC 2 reports cover control objectives and implementations; BYOK as a feature is more of a product offering. We'll document which controls are achieved when BYOK is enabled on Private, and which are not available on hosted without Private.
[07:02] Marcus: For vendor questionnaires we also ask about incident response SLA and RTO. What are Redwood's commitments?
[07:09] Jared: We have documented incident response procedures and notification timelines in the compliance pack. For Dedicated / Private customers we can agree SLAs in the contract; hosted customers get standard notification commitments.
[07:21] Dr. Naveen: Can you route notifications to our security mailbox and our PagerDuty?
[07:26] Jared: Yes, we can configure email and webhook / PagerDuty integrations for incident notifications.
[07:33] Emily: About personnel access: who has access to customer data? Need to know break-glass procedures and privileged user controls.
[07:40] Priya: Access is role-based and audited. We have privileged access reviews and break-glass policies documented. We'll include the control descriptions and evidence in the SOC pack.
[07:52] Marcus: A practical question: we have a procurement deadline end of Q1. If we start a pilot (POC) with Redwood Dedicated in January, will that affect the timeline for Private onboarding?
[07:59] Jared: Pilots on Dedicated are quicker - you can be up in weeks. Private involves more network setup and onboarding, so plan for a month or two depending on approvals.
[08:10] Emily: For the technical deep dive, can we focus on KMS/BYOK, log streaming, and RBAC mapping?
[08:15] Priya: Absolutely. We'll bring our infra engineer for that session.
[08:19] Dr. Naveen: Regarding controls mapping, will you map to our internal control IDs or do we map your controls to ours?
[08:25] Jared: We'll provide a mapping sheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 and ISO clauses; you can then link those to your internal control IDs. We can do a joint workshop to finalize.
[08:36] Marcus: On legal - are you comfortable with redlining certain security addendums around data residency and breach notifications?
[08:41] Jared: Yes, our legal team has standard security addendum templates. For enterprise contracts we negotiate specifics, especially around residency and breach timelines.
[08:50] Emily: One more question on encryption in transit: do you support mutual TLS for service-to-service calls?
[08:55] Priya: We support mTLS for Private and Dedicated components where you control the network. For hosted customers we use TLS with strong ciphers and cert rotation; mTLS is available for managed integrations.
[09:08] Jared: We're getting into good detail - let's summarize next steps: we'll share Trust Center link, SOC2 and ISO certs, controls mapping template, and schedule the technical deep dive. Marcus will send residency constraints.
[09:19] Emily: Sounds good. Any gotchas we should be aware of?
[09:23] Priya: Just the usual: hosted has some limitations around BYOK and full network isolation. If you need strict residency + BYOK + long retention you should be looking at Private. Also some physical controls are out of scope for hosted.
[09:36] Marcus: Regarding logging retention, the plan is to export to our S3 bucket; do you support encrypted delivery?
[09:42] Priya: Yes, logs can be delivered encrypted in transit and at rest. We can also sign uploads for integrity.
[09:48] Dr. Naveen: Let's talk timelines - after you send artifacts, our vendor team will take two weeks to review. If everything looks good, we'll schedule the technical deep dive.
[09:58] Jared: Perfect. We'll aim to get the Trust Center link and mapping within three business days. Priya will schedule the deep dive.
[10:06] Emily: Any examples of previous customers with similar requirements?
[10:09] Jared: We recently onboarded a health provider with similar PHI controls into Dedicated and then moved to Private for BYOK. Priya can share redacted control mappings.
[10:18] Priya: I'll prepare a redacted sample mapping.
[10:21] Marcus: For the technical session, please include network diagrams and data flow for inference requests.
[10:26] Priya: Yes, network diagrams and data flow, including where model weights live, will be included.
[10:31] Emily: One minor transcription issue - in our questionnaire we called out the need for 'immutable audit logs' - is that an explicit feature?
[10:38] Priya: We provide append-only audit streams and recommended retention to make them effectively immutable; for absolute immutability you'd pair with WORM storage on the customer side.
[10:48] Dr. Naveen: If Redwood were to provide copies of logs for an e-discovery request, what's the SLA?
[10:54] Jared: We can define e-discovery support in the contract; typically we can provide export within X business days - we'll confirm exact timing with legal.
[11:03] Emily: That should be fine.
[11:05] Marcus: Any final items from Redwood?
[11:08] Jared: We'll send the Trust Center link, controls mapping template, and sample event schema. We'll also propose two slots for the technical deep dive.
[11:15] Priya: I'll follow up with a calendar invite and attach the event schema and a redacted mapping sample.
[11:20] Dr. Naveen: Thanks all, we'll review the artifacts and get back.
[11:23] Emily: Thanks Jared and Priya. Bye.
[11:25] Jared: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
